"Anne Bülow" <bulow@essb.eur.nl>:
Dear Mohammad, Yesterday I’ve mailed you concerning our preparations for our big upcoming study. I came across some other issues that I hope you could help me with. Disable the “previous” button: In the surveys participants can navigate with a “previous” and “next” button (or whatever the original English translation is). For a specific questionnaire we don’t want participants to navigate back so that they cannot change their answer and end in another branched arm of the survey. Thus we want them to choose between A & B and not click on B look at it and go back and choose A and look at that. In the questionnaire settings and “Avicenna learn” I haven’t found any explanation about such an option, but assume that this is such a simple feature that you must have this for sure. Is it thus possible to disable the “previous” button? Display pictures in questionnaires (Apple): I have added some pictures to a questionnaire (study: 4080, survey: 22785). While I saw this picture on my phone (Android, Samsung), my colleague did not (IPhone). See screenshots attached. Could it be that there is a technical problem with IPhones or are only some picture formats supported by iOS? Do you know about this problem? Line breaks in data exports: Yesterday I tried to export the data (study 4080). I had difficulties opening the csv files properly. My analysis software (RStudio) gave the error message “more columns than column names”. Especially when inspecting the data files in the “old format”, I saw that there were line breaks in columnames when there was a line break in the item, which makes all the following column names the first data row (if you understand what I mean). I do not wish to remove all line breaks in the surveys as these are really useful to improve readability. I am wondering if the problem occurs at my end (when uploading the data) or that this is a “mistake” in the exporting function. That is, that when exporting it does not take the label (without line break) to make a column name, but the item itself. Thanks, Mohammad, for looking into this. I hope that for all the issues there is a quick fix that I have just overlooked. All the best, Anne Anne Bülow MSc PhD candidate/promovenda Youth & Family Erasmus School of Social and Behavioural Sciences W https://www.eur.nl/people/anne-bulow W https://www.paradoxscience.nl W https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Anne_Buelow Monday, Tuesday, Thursday & Friday
